newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ANGRY SPANISH FANS TO PROTEST WITH 15,000 WHISTLES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANGRY SPANISH FANS TO PROTEST WITH 15,000 WHISTLES.

text.p: Spanish Zaragoza fans armed with 15,000 whistles will give the referee at Saturday's home game against Athletic Bilbao a noisy reception in protest over a disputed penalty during last week's match with Barcelona.
On the advice of a linesman, the penalty was awarded by the match referee who sent off a Zaragoza defender. Barcelona then equalised on their way to a 5-3 victory.
Television replays suggested the decision was wrong and Zaragoza have launched an appeal to force a replay of the last twenty minutes of the game.

"We want our unhappiness to be known without violence...We also ask fans to bring along their own whistles. The more of us the better," said a representative of the Ligallo Fondo Norte supporters group, which will distribute the whistles.
Fans will add to the protest by displaying a giant banner, with references to the fateful -- and obscenity-charged -- conversation between referee and linesman.
The controversy seems to have stimulated interest in Zaragoza, where the first sell-out game of the season is expected.
